answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing and the 18% cost mandate is non-negotiable. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor has succeeded before with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. However, with the assembly line at 94% committed volume and only 14 days to contract expiration, this decision carries delivery risk. Verifying memory_c2 confirms the low-cost vendor's operational reliability. The assembly line has minimal buffer (6% slack), so switching must be executed cleanly with no migration delays. This is not a guarded test—the deadline forces a standard implementation. The decision is aggressive on cost but relies on proven vendor capability. Deferring is not viable (no auto-renewal); renewing locks in higher costs (incumbent refused price talks); adding a second source alone does not address the 18% mandate; renegotiating has already failed. Switching is the only path to cost target given the constraints.
